name: Czechia

income_tax.summary: Resident income tax is 15% up to CZK 1,762,812 (36x average monthly wage) and 23% above; no local income taxes. Employee share of insurance: 7.1% social (cap CZK 2,350,416 in 2026) and 4.5% health (no cap); the recorded rate is the combined 11.6% and the cap applies to the social part only.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Ordinary regime (derived effective rate on profit, recorded 22.81%): social insurance 29.2% (pension 28% plus 1.2% state employment policy, ČSSZ premium-rates page; sickness insurance 2.7% is voluntary and not included) on an assessment base of 55% of profit (the 55% share is from the statute as recalled and was NOT confirmed on an opened page; ČSSZ states only that the minimum base is 50% of the previous year's average tax base), giving about 16.06% of profit; health insurance 13.5% on a base of 50% of profit after expenses (VZP), giving 6.75%, minimum advance CZK 3,306 a month in 2026. The social cap (48x average wage, CZK 2,350,416) applies to the assessment base, not to profit, so it is not reached on EUR 54,000 or 130,000 of profit. In the flat-rate regime (income up to CZK 2m, not a VAT payer) the monthly payments for 2026 are CZK 9,162 (band I, income to 1m), 16,745 (band II, to 1.5m) and 27,139 (band III, to 2m), of which tax is 100 / 4,963 / 9,320, pension 5,756 / 8,191 / 12,527 and health 3,306 / 3,591 / 5,292. Lump-sum expense deductions in the ordinary regime: 80% (crafts, agriculture), 60% (some trades), 40%, 30% (rental), on a base of at most CZK 2m. Entrepreneurs may opt out of the sickness fund.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Taxpayer tax credit not stated by the PwC pages and not included, so personal_allowance is 0.

open_questions: The 55% pension assessment base share is not confirmed on an opened page (the 29.2% and 13.5% rates and the 50% health base are).
Annual taxpayer credit amount for 2026 is not stated by the PwC pages and was not read; personal_allowance stays 0.
The Financni sprava page and a podnikatel.cz article disagree on the band I amount (9,162 vs 9,984); the tax authority page says 9,162 applies retroactively from 1 January 2026.

regimes.name: Flat-rate regime (pausalni rezim) for self-employed
regimes.description: Fixed monthly payment covering income tax, pension and health insurance: CZK 9,162 (band I), 16,745 (band II), 27,139 (band III) in 2026. Requires income up to CZK 2 million (band limits 1m / 1.5m / 2m, higher for 60%-80% expense activities), not a VAT payer, and limits on dependent-work income.
regimes.duration_note: Open-ended while income and VAT conditions hold.

residence_routes: EU citizens can live and work freely and register a trade or employment. Non-EU nationals, including US citizens, need a long-term visa or permit: an employee card or blue card for skilled employees, or a long-term residence for business (trade licence) for freelancers; conditions were not verified from an official page.
